assessment: No blocking defect found in the inspected optional-filter behavior.

checks: nil final filter preserves historical last-match behavior
nil fragment filter preserves historical first-business stop
final ACK never calls business filter
all continuation ACK heads preserve fragment sequencing
wrong fragment ACK after a notification stops before next write
coalesced early rejection ACK and notification stop remaining writes
filter throw after candidate reply rejects complete read
notification alone cannot acknowledge request fragment
notifications do not hide duplicate accepted replies
different-event business message is routed without passing response filter
late duplicated prior reply routes to unsolicited on next event

correct: Coalesced matching main reply is retained while same-key settled notifications route to unsolicited, regardless of their position in the read.
Empty fragment ACKs bypass the business filter and intermediate ACK heads remain checked.
An accepted early business reply returns before any remaining request fragment is written. A malformed filter result throws, with no retry.
Two filter-accepted business replies in the same decoded read are rejected even with intervening notifications.
Nil filter preserves historical final-read last-match selection and intermediate first-business return.
limits: The filter only sees matching event/service/command business messages. Different-event messages and late duplicates route to nonthrowing unsolicited.
Client should returnfalse only for validated notifications; native rejections must returntrue or throw to prevent later fragment writes.
An unsolicited validator can record an error flag; live caller must check it before further commands because callback itself cannotthrow.
No extra drain occurs after accepted reply. Duplicate detection is bounded to one decoded read and is explicitly documented; nextread may see late notifications.
Generic session has no poisoned-state flag; caller controls recovery after a thrown error.
